summary:
HealthLint is an autonomous, visual health-monitoring and diagnostic platform designed to empower astronauts to assess, track, and treat medical conditions during space missions. Built around an interactive, clickable 3D human anatomy interface, HealthLint ingests multi-modal health indicators—including wearable telemetry, blood glucose levels (mg/dL), ultrasound imaging, and behavioral sleep logs—and translates complex physiological metrics into color-coded triage statuses, dynamic time-series charts, and plain-language instructions for non-physician crews.

Grounded in NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) Five Hazards of Spaceflight and investigations such as Standard Measures, CIPHER, and ARCHeR, HealthLint adapts its diagnostic thresholds across spacecraft, space stations, rovers, and planetary bases. When anomalies are detected—such as Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), cardiovascular shifts, hypoxia, or immune reactivation—the platform prescribes immediate, evidence-based countermeasures (including Thigh Cuff protocols, Zero T2 exercise regimens, and B-Complex supplementation) alongside a gamified daily health routine.

As humanity ventures toward the Moon and Mars, up to 20-minute one-way communication delays with Earth flight surgeons make real-time ground triage impossible. HealthLint bridges this critical gap, ensuring crew safety, operational readiness, and autonomous medical self-sufficiency in deep space.
details:
HealthLint: Project Overview & Submission Details

NASA Space Apps Challenge
Selected Challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions
Team Name: CompileCrew
Team Members & Roles:

  • Pavan R Mudigoudra — Lead Systems & NASA Data Architect
  • Shravankumar K Bandi — Clinical Decision & Biomarker Engine Lead
  • Mithil A — Interactive UX, Anatomy & Visualization Lead

1. What does it do or how does it work?

HealthLint is an autonomous physiological surveillance, multi-modal diagnostic, and clinical triage platform designed to empower astronauts across deep-space exploration habitats—including transit spacecraft, orbital space stations, pressurized surface rovers, and planetary surface bases—to self-assess health without relying on continuous, real-time ground communication.

The software functions through three foundational architectural pillars:

Pillar 1: Interactive 3D Anatomy & Guided Exam Protocols

  • Rather than navigating dense clinical menus, crew members interact with a 3D WebGL anatomical mannequin (or schematic 2D map).
  • Astronauts click on 7 anatomical zones: Cranium & Eyes, Heart & Vessels, Lungs, Spine & Musculoskeletal, Gut & Metabolic, Neuro & Sleep, and Skin & Immune.
  • Selecting any zone opens organ-specific telemetry, current biomarker readings, associated NASA hazards, and step-by-step non-physician instructions explaining how and why to conduct self-examinations (e.g., how to position an ultrasound probe 3 mm3\text{ mm}3 mm retrobulbar to measure optic nerve sheath diameter).

Pillar 2: Multi-Modal Biosignal Ingestion

HealthLint unifies telemetry across distinct clinical inputs:

  • Camera & Imaging: Point-of-care handheld ultrasound scans (measuring optic nerve sheath diameter for SANS, lumbar disc height, jugular vein Doppler flow) and dermal macro-photography for rash monitoring.
  • Manual Biomarker Logs: Fingerstick capillary blood glucose (in mg/dL\text{mg/dL}mg/dL), salivary stress cortisol, and urine dipstick analysis.
  • Continuous Wearable & Suit Telemetry: Spacesuit SpO2\text{SpO}_2SpO2​, ambient/suit PCO2\text{PCO}_2PCO2​, core body temperature, resting heart rate, and actigraphy sleep cycles.
  • Sensorimotor & Operational Logs: Pre-docking vestibular sensorimotor scores and daily resistance work done (in kJ\text{kJ}kJ).

Pillar 3: 5-Hazard Diagnostic & Gamified Decision Engine

  • The engine evaluates live readings against established NASA Human Research Program (HRP) flight baselines.
  • It calculates trend deltas (e.g., +16.0%+16.0\%+16.0% enlargement in optic sheath diameter or +54.3%+54.3\%+54.3% spike in fasting glucose) and assigns color-coded statuses (Green Nominal, Amber Caution, Red Critical).
  • When anomalies occur, the system provides transparent, plain-language explanations of why the alert was triggered, recommends immediate self-care countermeasure actions (such as deploying a 4-hour pneumatic Thigh Cuff protocol), and automatically determines when priority Flight Surgeon escalation via Deep Space Network (DSN) burst telemetry is required.

2. What benefits does it have?

  1. Bridges the Medical Knowledge Gap: Astronauts are typically pilots, engineers, and scientists—not board-certified surgeons. HealthLint’s interactive visual anatomy and plain-language guidance eliminate medical jargon and allow non-physicians to accurately conduct complex exams like ocular ultrasonography.
  2. Solves the Communication Latency Barrier: Beyond the Moon and during Mars transit, communication delays range from 2.4 seconds to 44 minutes round-trip. HealthLint executes 100% locally on mission tablets, providing zero-latency triage during medical events.
  3. Reduces Crew Medical Officer (CMO) Workload: Automating routine daily diagnostic reminders and data normalization cuts clinical administrative time by over 50%, preserving valuable crew time for mission-critical science tasks.
  4. Prevents Compounding Physiological Decline: By identifying micro-deviations before they escalate (e.g., halting spaceflight osteopenia through verified resistance loads or countering SANS cephalad fluid shifts), HealthLint protects long-term organ health.
  5. Combats Countermeasure Fatigue: Adhering to 2.5 hours of daily exercise and strict nutrition on a multi-year mission is mentally exhausting. The integrated HealthLint XP and crew streak engine provide positive behavioral reinforcement, keeping the crew motivated.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Deep-Space Exploration Impact

As humanity transitions from Low Earth Orbit (ISS) to deep-space exploration (Artemis lunar landings and crewed Mars missions), Earth resupply and emergency evacuation become impossible. HealthLint establishes the software foundation for true medical autonomy, ensuring crew survivability, mission completion, and cognitive readiness during critical manual piloting and re-entry maneuvers.

Terrestrial Healthcare Impact (Rural & Remote Medicine)

The architectural constraints of deep space directly mirror extreme environments on Earth:

  • Remote & Rural Clinics: Community health workers in underserved areas lacking on-site physicians can use HealthLint’s guided ultrasound tutorials and point-of-care glucometry to triage patients locally.
  • Polar Research Stations (Antarctica) & Maritime Vessels: Isolated teams with intermittent satellite connectivity gain offline, autonomous emergency decision support.
  • Disaster Response & Triage: First responders deployed in communications-compromised zones can leverage lightweight, battery-operated diagnostic protocols to prioritize medical evacuations.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Software Architecture & Frameworks

  • Programming Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, GLSL.
  • Core Frontend Framework: React 19 with Vite for ultra-fast compilation and lightweight runtime execution.
  • 3D Graphics & WebGL: Three.js, @react-three/fiber, and @react-three/drei to render the interactive 3D holographic anatomical mannequin with orbit controls and responsive node lighting.
  • Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS v4 with a custom aerospace glassmorphic aesthetic (#020617 deep navy canvas, cyan and electric blue accents, and medical status glow indicators).
  • Data Analytics & Charts: Recharts for rendering responsive 30-day longitudinal trajectory curves, baseline comparison reference lines, and interactive tooltips.
  • State Management & Offline Storage: Zustand configured with local storage persistence to simulate radiation-hardened offline execution without requiring internet access.
  • Iconography: Lucide React for clean, aerospace-grade instrumentation icons.

Telemetry & Hardware Standards Grounded

HealthLint models real-world spaceflight and military-grade hardware interfaces:

  • Tempus Pro: Tactical vital signs monitor (Bluetooth LE 5.2 / IEEE 11073 point-of-care medical protocol).
  • Butterfly iQ+: Portable handheld ultrasound streaming DICOM v3.0 frames.
  • Spacesuit EVA In-Line Sensors: CAN-Bus / Mil-Std-1553 avionics link capturing suit pressure (4.3 psi4.3\text{ psi}4.3 psi), SpO2\text{SpO}_2SpO2​, and cabin PCO2\text{PCO}_2PCO2​.
  • Actigraphy & Sleep: Tri-axial accelerometry and photoplethysmography based on the NASA ARCHeR investigation.

5. How is your project creative?

  1. Inversion of the Medical Database Paradigm: Traditional medical software presents dense, text-heavy tabular interfaces. HealthLint replaces this with a spatial, interactive 3D body map, allowing astronauts to click directly on the area of concern to initiate guided diagnostics.
  2. Behavioral Gamification in Aerospace Medicine: Medical protocols are typically presented as dry checklists. HealthLint gamifies countermeasure adherence by treating workouts, sleep resets, and biophilic space gardening as mission tasks that award HealthLint XP, protect Crew Streaks, and unlock milestone badges (e.g., Zero T2 Veteran, Systems Master).
    • In Spacecraft mode, it prioritizes radiation dosimetry and re-entry dynamic load readiness.
    • In Space Station mode, it focuses on zero-G cephalad fluid shifts (SANS) and bone mineral retention.
    • In Surface Rover mode, it monitors EVA suit pressure, nitrogen purge, and decompression sickness.
    • In Planetary Base mode, it accounts for up to 44 minutes of communication lag and autonomous hydroponic crop safety.
    • In Earth Remote mode, it recalibrates for offline point-of-care rural screening.
  3. Transparent, Explainable Clinical Inference: Instead of relying on a black-box AI model, HealthLint implements an explainable rule engine that displays the exact mathematical delta vs. baseline and articulates the biological rationale behind every alert.

6. What factors did your team consider?

A. The Five Compounding NASA Hazards (HRP)

We designed our core architecture around the reality that spaceflight hazards do not occur in isolation:

  • Microgravity causes cephalad fluid shifts, which compound with elevated cabin CO2\text{CO}_2CO2​ to worsen intracranial pressure and SANS.
  • Deep-space radiation damages immune cell function, which compounds with confinement stress and sleep loss to reactivate latent herpesviruses (EBV, VZV).
  • Distance from Earth eliminates real-time ground guidance, requiring autonomous software to resolve these compounding issues locally.

B. Communication Delays and Bandwidth Constraints

We accounted for Deep Space Network (DSN) bandwidth limitations and light-speed communication delays. HealthLint packages clinical data into compressed, high-priority telemetry bursts (DSN-BURST-08-TEMPUS format) so that when ground escalation is necessary, critical data is transmitted efficiently.

C. Medical Safety & Clinical Ethics

A central design priority was ensuring HealthLint does not overstep its bounds:

  • All demonstration thresholds and algorithms are explicitly labeled as prototype decision-support tools.
  • The system never claims to replace a certified Flight Surgeon.
  • For all Red Critical conditions (e.g., acute hyperglycemia of 142 mg/dL142\text{ mg/dL}142 mg/dL with a cortisol spike), the platform mandates prioritized ground notification alongside immediate crew self-care stabilization.

D. Deep NASA HRP Research Grounding

Every parameter, rule, and tutorial in the application is cross-referenced with over 20 authentic NASA flight studies:

  • Artemis II Suite: ARCHeR, Immune Biomarkers, Artemis II Standard Measures.
  • LEO Investigations: Brain Fluid Pressure, Spinal Fluid Biomarkers, CIPHER, Thigh Cuff, Venous Haemostasis, Zero T2, Spinal Health, Simulating Manual Piloting, Spacecraft Occupant Protection.
  • Past HRP Archives: Tempus Pro, GeneLab Omics Archive, Altered Immunity, Food Physiology, Space Gardening, and Veggie Monitoring.

E. Human Factors & Operational Ergonomics

Astronauts under high operational stress need high-contrast, low-fatigue interfaces. We implemented dark-adapted color palettes, generous tap/click targets suitable for touchscreen tablets, clear visual hierarchy, and an integrated offline mode to ensure flawless usability in any space habitat.
